title: Using single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry to count RNA molecules in single cells in zebrafish embryos
protocol: Wait until embryos reach the 12–14 somite stage.
Thaw one aliquot of 4% PFA and ensure it is at 20°C–25°C.
Check GFP signal and morphology under a fluorescence microscope.
Remove embryos with abnormal morphology or weak GFP signal.
Select 15 embryos for each experimental condition.
Transfer selected embryos into a 2 mL tube.
Remove excess water from the embryos.
Rinse embryos once with 1 mL of 4% PFA.
Add 2 mL of 4% PFA to the embryos.
Cover the tube to keep embryos in dark conditions.
Shake the tube containing embryos for 1 hour at 20°C–25°C.
Remove unnecessary multipoints in case corner tiles are free of tissue.
Select tissue format in every 5 slices using manual surface creation.
Create a surface to mask DAPI (nucleus).
Create a surface to mask FITC (membrane) channels.
Use “Mask All” in the “Tab Edit”.
Set voxel intensity outside surface to zero “0”.
Split image into four images using “Crop 3D”.
Add X and Y data of the points in the "Somite" sheet of the left-anterior XLS file.
Add X and Y data of the points in the "Somite" sheet of the right-anterior XLS file.
Measure angle of expression stripes along the posterior-anterior axis for different wild-type samples.
Plot an "Angle vs Distance (μm)" graph to fit an equation.
Determine delta_angle from the slope of the fitted equation.
Determine angle from the Y-intercept of the fitted equation.
Check transparency of embryos under dissecting microscope after approximately 45 minutes of fixation.
Remove PFA if embryos are not transparent.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL PBST-0.1%.
Add 2 mL PBST-0.1% and shake slowly for 5 minutes.
Mix 3 mL PBST-0.1% and 3 mL methanol into a petri dish.
Dechorionate embryos in the mixture for 5 minutes in a dark room.
Transfer embryos back to the tube after dechorionation.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL methanol.
Add 2 mL methanol and shake slowly for 5 minutes.
Refresh medium with 2 mL methanol.
Store the tube at -20°C for 24 hours.
Transfer embryos to a 1.5 mL flat bottom microcentrifuge tube using a glass pipette.
Remove methanol from the tube as much as possible without touching or damaging the embryos.
First, remove most of the methanol with a 1000 μL filtered tip until less than 250 μL remains.
Then hold the tube tilted and remove the remaining solution along the side of the tube to avoid touching the embryos.
Air dry the embryos by leaving the tube open for methanol evaporation until they no longer contact each other (∼5–20 min).
Add 1 drop of RNAscope Protease-III pre-treatment solution to the tube.
Gently tap the tube to sink the embryos down.
Wait for 20 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL PBST-0.01% gently.
Add 1 mL PBST-0.01%.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 5 min.
Repeat the previous step for 2 more times.
Remove all solution.
Add fresh 250 μL prehybridization buffer.
Place tube in a box with a 45° tilted position.
Incubate at 40°C for 2 hours.
Ensure all probes are completely dissolved.
Remove all solution from the tube.
Add 15 μL probe mixture to the tube.
Gently tap the tube to mix.
Place the tube vertically in a box.
Incubate the tube at 40°C for 16 hours.
Make sure all embryos are in a row at the bottom of the tube.
Prepare 50 mL SSCT (0.2× SSC, 0.01% Tween 20).
Place 4% PFA at 20°C–25°C.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL SSCT.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 15 min.
Repeat the previous step for 4 more times.
Remove all SSCT.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL 4% PFA.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 10 min.
Remove 4% PFA as much as possible.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL SSCT.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 15 min.
Repeat the previous step for 2 more times.
Remove all SSCT from the tube.
Add one drop of Amp 1 (∼20 μL) and tap gently to sink embryos down.
Place the tube vertically and incubate at 40°C for 30 minutes.
Rinse with 1 mL SSCT.
Shake the tube slowly in a horizontal position for 15 minutes.
Repeat the previous step four more times.
Take Amp 2 out to 20°C–25°C for 30 minutes before applying it.
Remove all SSCT from the tube.
Add one drop of Amp 2 (∼20 μL) and tap gently to sink embryos down.
Place the tube vertically and incubate at 40°C for 15 minutes.
Rinse with 1 mL SSCT.
Shake the tube slowly in a horizontal position for 15 minutes.
Repeat the previous step two more times.
Take Amp 3 out to 20°C–25°C for 30 minutes before applying it.
Remove all SSCT from the tube.
Add one drop of Amp 3 (∼20 μL) and tap gently to sink embryos down.
Place the tube vertically and incubate at 40°C for 30 minutes.
Rinse with 1 mL SSCT.
Shake the tube slowly in a horizontal position for 15 minutes.
Take Amp 4 Alt B out to 20°C–25°C for 30 minutes before applying it.
Choose Amp 4 Alt B to label probes with different fluorophores.
Tap gently to sink embryos down after adding one drop of Amp 4 Alt B (∼20 μL).
Incubate tube vertically in an oven at 40°C for 15 minutes covered with aluminum foil.
Rinse with 1 mL SSCT and shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 15 minutes.
Repeat rinsing step with 1 mL SSCT two more times.
Remove all SSCT after final rinse.
Rinse embryos with 1 mL of 4% PFA, then add 1 mL of 4% PFA.
Store embryos and reagents at 4°C for 16 hours.
Mix 5 mL of 10× PBS with approximately 30 mL DEPC water.
Add 500 μL of Triton X-100 to the mixture.
Top up to 50 mL with DEPC water on the next day and mix well.
Top up PBSTX to 50 mL that was prepared the day before in the afternoon (∼1–2 pm).
Final concentration would be 1× PBS 1% Triton X-100.
Remove 4% PFA.
Rinse with 1 mL PBSTX.
Add 1 mL PBSTX.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 5 min.
Prepare permeabilization buffer (995 μL PBSTX + 5 μL Triton X-100 for each tube).
Repeat the previous step for 2 more times.
Remove PBSTX after rinsing twice.
Add 1 mL permeabilization buffer.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare blocking buffer (PBSTXBG): 0.2 g BSA + 10 mL PBSTX + 100 μL GS.
Remove permeabilization buffer after incubation.
Add 1 mL PBSTXBG.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 2 h at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare primary antibody solution: 180 μL PBSTXBG + 1 μL Chicken anti-GFP.
Store the rest of PBSTXBG at 4°C.
Remove PBSTXBG as much as possible (probably 20 μL left).
Add 180 μL primary antibody solution.
Final concentration would be 1:200 (10 μg/mL).
Shake tube slowly with a 45° tilt position for 20–24 h at 4°C in a cold room.
Start secondary antibody staining afternoon (∼4 pm) on the fifth day of experiment.
Remove primary antibody solution.
Rinse with 1 mL PBSTX.
Add 1 mL PBSTX.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Repeat the previous step for 2 more times.
Remove PBSTX.
Add 1 mL PBSTXBG.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare secondary antibody solution: Mix 380 μL PBSTXBG with 2 μL Alexa Fluor 488 anti-Chicken and 1.1 μL Hoechst 33342 per tube.
Remove PBSTXBG as much as possible (approximately 20 μL left).
Add 380 μL secondary antibody solution to the sample.
Shake tube slowly with a 45° tilt position for 16 h at 4°C in a cold room.
Remove secondary antibody solution after incubation.
Rinse and wash embryos once with SSCT.
Shake tube slowly in a horizontal position for 7 min at 4°C in a cold room.
Rinse and add 1 mL 4% PFA to the sample.
Place one embryo into a petri dish using a transfer pipette.
Cut from the head with a microsurgical knife.
Make little cuts on the skin to remove yolk from the tissue.
Use a lash tool to gently remove excess yolk.
Continue cutting until presomitic mesoderm (PSM) and 1–2 somites are left.
Remove all remaining yolk to ensure PSM integrity.
Place one drop of ProLong Gold antifade reagent on a glass slide.
Transfer the tissue into the reagent using a lash tool.
Ensure the tissue is dorsoventrally flattened.
Apply transparent nail polish and fix with a coverslip gently.
Wait for 5 minutes for the nail polish to dry before starting imaging.
Place specimen onto the stage.
Put oil onto the lens of 100× objective.
Find focus plane by ocular lenses.
Check nucleus (Hoechst) and membrane (GFP) signal at the most anterior part of the tissue.
Determine appropriate laser power and PMT HV.
Open Acquire>Scan Large Image.
Select “Left, top, right and bottom limits” in the Area panel.
Set stitching overlap as 5%.
In the DAPI channel (for nucleus), run the Live camera.
Locate sample’s XY limits.
Set Z range at positions where there is no signal using Top and Bottom buttons in the Z panel in the ND Acquisition window.
Press Home (middle Z position).
Go to symmetric mode and press Relative button.
Go to middle XY position and close “Scan Large Image” window.
Note the number of X and Y fields.
Go to XY panel in the ND Acquisition window.
Select “include Z”.
Press Custom button.
Under the Large Image section, select 100× objective.
Write the number of X and Y fields.
Set overlap area as 5%.
Deselect any multipoint if it doesn’t include the tissue because of rotated sample mounting.
Add optical configurations to the λ (multichannel) panel in the ND Acquisition window.
Run image analysis between 2 to 7 days after imaging.
Prepare images for analysis by creating surface, masking and cell segmentation.
Open multipoint ND2 file in NIS Elements.
Go to “Image > ND Processing > Stitch Multipoint to Large Image”.
Stitch multipoints via blending without shading correction.
Save the stitched file.
Use “Imaris File Converter” to convert stitched ND2 file to IMS file.
Open IMS file in Imaris software.
Use “Surface” wizard to mask nucleus and membrane of the tissue.
In the 3D view, select “Surfaces”.
Skip automatic surface creation and click edit manually.
Choose “Manual” resolution with highest X-Y size.
Turn on “slicer rendering for selected object”.
Click "Draw" and select the region of interest in every 5 slices from top to bottom of the image.
If the tissue borders change dramatically along the z-axis, select the tissue borders in every 2–3 slices instead of 5.
Select precisely from the border of the PSM cells.
Include adaxial cells in the PSM and S1 somite.
Exclude notochord, neural tube, and skin cells.
Click "Create Surface".
Choose Nucleus channel and set voxel intensity outside surface to zero.
Repeat it for Membrane channel too.
Deselect “Duplicate channel before applying mask” if selected outside of the tissue.
Rotate the image from "Image Processing > Free Rotate" to make it horizontal view from anterior to posterior by using an appropriate angle.
Set X and Y axis as “0” and Z axis as “1” in the rotation axis.
Split the image into four images from “Edit > Crop 3D”.
Rename files of the left-anterior, left-posterior, right anterior, and right-posterior parts as ending “_LA”, “_LP”, “_RA”, and “_RP”, respectively.
Click “add new cells” for cell segmentation.
Select detection type as "Detect Nucleus, Cell and Vesicles".
Select nucleus channel.
Set nucleus diameter as 3 μm.
Apply smoothing (filter width 0.3 μm).
Apply background subtraction (sphere diameter 1.2 μm).
Split nuclei by seed points.
Set automatic nuclei threshold (background subtraction).
Filter nuclei with “Nucleus Number of Voxels” between 8543 and 67800.
Select cell detection type as "Detect Cell Boundary from Cell Membrane".
Set "cell smallest diameter" as 0.25 μm.
Set "membrane detail" as zero.
Apply “Cell Volume” filter between 150 μm³ and 450 μm³.
For each vesicle type, select channels for each RNA.
Set estimated diameter as 0.5 μm.
Apply background subtraction.
Add “quality” filter to detect one vesicle for each single RNA punctum.
Add a “Measurement Point” in the Surpass Tree list of the left-anterior and right-anterior files.
Find anterior borders of the PSM tissue in each sample.
Create “Somite” sheet in all anterior files (i.e., “TITLE_LA.xls” and “TITLE_RA.xls”).
Add X-Y positions of two points in Cell A2-B2 for “Point A” and Cell A3-B3 for “Point B” in the “Somite” sheet.
Measure angle and distance from the tail end of expression stripes of the segmentation clock in the PSM in all embryos in each genetic background.
Fit an equation to the data, i.e., “Angle_vs_Distance = delta_angle ∗ Distance + angle”.
Transfer all XLS files into “XLS_to_XLSX” folder.
Convert XLS files to XLSX format using “xlsToxlsxIMARIS.py”.
Transfer anterior XLSX files (i.e., “TITLE_LA.xlsx” and “TITLE_RA.xlsx”) into “Anterior” folder.
Transfer posterior XLSX files (i.e., “TITLE_LP.xlsx” and “TITLE_RP.xlsx”) into “Posterior” folder.
Run “separatePSM_volume_Green_farred.m” in the “Anterior” folder to calculate background from anterior files using MATLAB.
Run “combineLRP_volume.m” in the “Posterior” folder to combine sheets using MATLAB.
Transfer "TITLE_LA_PSM.xlsx", "TITLE_RA_PSM.xlsx", "TITLE_LP_PSM.xlsx", and "TITLE_RP_PSM.xlsx" files into a "MergedPSM" folder.
Merge the transferred files using "merge_excel_FileInDirectory_wo_Vol.py" for without volume correction.
Merge the transferred files using "merge_excel_FileInDirectory_w_Vol.py" for with volume corrected RNA levels.
Check background values at “bgSomiteCount.xlsx”.
Copy and paste raw values from columns B-E of either left or right anterior files into “SampleInfo.xlsx” file in the “Input” folder for without volume corrected excel files.
Copy and paste volume-corrected values from columns F-I of either left or right anterior files into “SampleInfo.xlsx” file in the “Input” folder for with volume corrected excel files.
Rename "TITLE_merged_w_Vol_PSM.xlsx" and "TITLE_merged_wo_Vol_PSM.xlsx" files with ascending order numbers ending like “TITLE_wv_#.xlsx” or “TITLE_wov_#.xlsx”.
Transfer renamed files into the same “Input” folder together with “SampleInfo.xlsx” file.
Edit “Python name” in Column B in the “SampleInfo.xlsx” file according to “TITLE_wv_#.xlsx” or “TITLE_wov_#.xlsx” filenames like “TITLE_wv_#” or “TITLE_wov_#”.
Run “GENOTYPE_wVol.py” and “GENOTYPE_woVol.py” for each genetic background.
Correct folder paths and filename formats in the python code.
If there is no stripy expression, use wild-type’s angle of expression (41.381) and angle variation slope (0.0403).
Run “COMPARE_GENETICBACKGROUNDS.py” to compare transcriptional variabilities of different genetic backgrounds.

Format: python COMPARE_GENETICBACKGROUNDS.py <number of genetic backgrounds> <number of bins for noise plots> <comparison outcome folder> <folders containing files to be compared (i.e., directory of “Output” folders of each genotype)> <genetic background names for labeling> <genetic background colors for plotting>.
